beats.text: Footsteps on the stairs, in the middle of the night. That's what a former curator reported at the White River Light Station, near Whitehall, Michigan.
beats.label: NEAR WHITEHALL, MICHIGAN

beats.text: The lighthouse was built in 1875 and first lit in May 1876. Its first keeper was Captain William Robinson, who came from England.
beats.label: FIRST LIT 1876
beats.credit: Lighthousefriends; U.S. Coast Guard Historian's Office

beats.text: He and his wife, Sarah, had 13 children. He kept the light for more than 40 years.
beats.label: MORE THAN 40 YEARS

beats.text: In 1919, at 87, he was retired, and his grandson took over as keeper. That same spring, the old captain died.
beats.label: SPRING 1919

beats.text: People say he never left. Guests and staff have reported footsteps upstairs, and the tap of a cane.
beats.label: WHAT PEOPLE REPORT

beats.text: The light was shut off in 1960. Since 1970, it has been a museum.
beats.label: A MUSEUM SINCE 1970
beats.credit: U.S. Coast Guard Historian's Office; Lighthousefriends

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
